text:
arun: Heads-up — after the eu-west2 kernel image roll (5.15 -> 6.4.12) ~30% of P4 hosts are failing to load the NVIDIA module during boot. Provisioner + autoscaler backlog is climbing, nodes stay NotReady and pods sit Pending.

marta: Ugh. Symptoms? modprobe errors / dmesg?

arun: Quick log excerpt from one bad host:
```
[    3.512345] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[    3.512349] nvidia: Unknown symbol: nv_usm_alloc (err -22)
[    3.512350] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
[    3.512351] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
```

kai: `disagrees about version of symbol module_layout` usually DKMS or mismatched driver. Which driver release?

arun: We're on driver 535.86.05 baked into the node image. CUDA 12.2. The same image worked on 5.15 in canary yesterday. Problem appears only on some hardware variants (p4d vs p4) and some hosts finish modprobe but later show NCCL handshake timeouts.

lee: Are we seeing any kernel oops / panic? Or just module load failures and then k8s readiness failing?

arun: No full panics. But multiple nodes go NotReady because `nvidia-smi` is missing -> kubelet marks container runtime degraded -> kube-proxy flaps. Also saw a few oom-killer events on gpu-scheduler process when it tried to query /dev/nvidiactl repeatedly.

joanne: Impact: provisioning is slow -> autoscaler is spamming API calls -> costs going up because we keep creating VM requests that never become Ready. Any quick mitigation?

arun: Short-term: pin new node pools to kernel 5.15 images, stop the 6.4 rollout. We throttled the autoscaler and added a taint `gpu.upgrade/incompatible=true:NoSchedule` to the affected nodepool images to prevent scheduling.

marta: Can we hotfix by rebuilding DKMS on the 6.4 images? Maybe module ABI changed and DKMS build against headers failed silently. Check `/var/lib/dkms/*/build/make.log`.

arun: Already checked — DKMS modules appear to have built but the produced .ko has different vermagic. Example: `vermagic: 6.4.12` vs the running kernel `6.4.12-rt`? There's a mismatch in local kernel flavor on some hosts (rt vs generic).

kai: That would explain host-to-host variability. Some of our images have `-rt` preempt patches for latency. Did the node image pipeline accidentally mix kernel flavors?

arun: Looks like yesterday's AMI bake produced two images: `eu-west2-p4-6.4-generic` and `eu-west2-p4-6.4-rt`. Provisioner registered both under the same nodepool label.

lee: Oof. Next step: tag the bad AMI and roll back. Also, can we make the provisioner filter by kernel flavor until we rebuild?

joanne: Cost note: we're seeing a 12% increase in active VMs waiting for Ready. If rollback takes 2 hours we'll be billed for those. We might want to temporarily expand burst capacity elsewhere (us-west) to take load while eu-west2 recovers.

arun: Agreed. Also noticed NCCL timeouts between mixed-kernel nodes: random `nccl: handshake timed out` entries in pod logs. Might be caused by partial module loads (some nodes missing features) causing topology mismatch.

marta: For triage: 1) isolate and cordon bad flavor, 2) snapshot DKMS build logs on failing hosts, 3) reproduce locally by booting 6.4-rt in lab p4 node. I'll take #2 and #3.

kai: I'll coordinate rollback and AMI tagging. Preparing a revert to 5.15 image set and draining 6.4 nodes.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-023 — Kernel 6.4 launch causing GPU module incompatibility in eu-west2. Pager: eng-oncall. Severity: P2.

lee: Quick workaround for running workloads: add a nodeSelector to critical deployments to prefer managed 5.15 nodepool. Also update autoscaler to ignore nodepool that is `gpu.upgrade/incompatible`.

joanne: I'm running a cost calc: if we keep 50 pending VMs for 3h at 7$/hr each, that's ~1050 USD wasted — don't let provisioning keep spinning.

arun: We're also seeing modprobe race on boot: sometimes firmware loading completes after kernel module load attempt, causing missing symbols. Proposed: add a `modprobe --retry` wrapper at early-boot to wait for firmware readiness, but that's a bit fragile.

marta: I'd rather rebuild AMIs consistently than patch boot scripts. Root cause is image drift. We need stricter AMI bake validations: check vermagic using the kernel headers package and failing bake if mismatch.

kai: Agree. Immediate plan: 
- rollback eu-west2 nodepools to 5.15 (kai)
- cordon/tag bad 6.4-rt AMI (kai)
- triage DKMS/build logs and reproduce in lab (marta)
- update autoscaler config to avoid bad nodepool (lee)
- monitor NCCL errors and mark impact (arun)

joanne: Assigning owners and ETA?

arun: I'll monitor NCCL error curve and post updates. ETA for rollback: 45–90m depending on kube drain.

marta: Repro + logs by EOD; if I can reproduce in lab I can prepare a proper fix for DKMS.

kai: Rolling back now — starting drains. Will update with progress.

oncall-bot: Update: INC-2026-023 status changed to mitigated by rollback.

arun: Post-rollback notes: after draining and replacing 6.4 nodes with 5.15, Pending pod count dropped to normal, autoscaler queue cleared. No more NCCL handshake errors on the replaced nodes.

lee: Action item: add AMI validation gate for `module_layout` vermagic and kernel flavor consistency. Ticketed in infra backlog: INFRA-1427.

marta: Also add a small test in the bake CI: run `modinfo nvidia` and `nvidia-smi` in a booted container image to detect early failures.

joanne: Cost/ops follow-up: retro on provisioning thresholds — we should fail fast instead of queuing VMs for incompatible nodepools.

arun: Thanks everyone. Please ping if you see any residual NotReady hosts.

kai: Update 30m later: drains completed, 6.4 nodepool scaled to 0, rolling back AMI tags. Will lock 6.4 bake until we have a tested fix.

marta: Filed DKMS investigation PR with notes and a sample `vermagic` mismatch log.

lee: Closing loop: monitor for recurrence when we retry kernel upgrade with stricter AMI checks. :thumbsup:
